title: China Robotaxis Face Losses as Utilization Trails Waymo, BI Says
key_facts: Bloomberg Intelligence (BI) expects Pony AI and WeRide, two Chinese robotaxi companies, to keep making operating losses through 2028.
BI ties the losses to lower use of each car compared with Waymo, whose utilization BI puts at more than 58 percent.
The weaker use pushes back the point at which the Chinese firms can break even.
BI says Waymo’s utilization held steady as it added cars and only improved when the average trip got longer.
BI analyst Robin Leung: robotaxi fleets have to reach densities that are convenient for passengers, otherwise high overheads weigh on margins.
BI says neither Chinese operator is on track to reach the needed domestic fleet density until later in the 2020s.
With local commercial growth hitting snags this year, both are exploring expansion in the Middle East and Europe, where rules are friendlier.
quote_evidence: Bloomberg Intelligence expects Pony AI and WeRide to keep logging operating losses through 2028.
This suggests robotaxi fleets have to reach densities that are convenient for passengers.
Without these densities, high overheads will continue to weigh on margins for both Pony AI and WeRide.
why_it_matters_hint: Robotaxi profit depends on how busy each car is and how dense the fleet is, so Chinese firms face a long road to break-even and are looking abroad.
